detail.body:
- Engram tables docs: the `peer_read` example sets attention DP with `--attn-dp-size 8` instead of the deprecated `--dp-size 8 --enable-dp-attention`.
- `EnvField.override` restores the variable in a `finally`, so an exception inside the `with` block no longer leaves the override set for later code and tests.

No behavior change, except that an env override is now undone when its block raises.

files.patch:
@@ -34,8 +34,8 @@ sglang serve --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tp-size 4 \
   --engram-config '{"placement": "cpu"}'
 
 # Rows in GPU memory, read from the owning GPU without a collective.
-sglang serve --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tp-size 8 --dp-size 8 \
-  --enable-dp-attention --engram-config '{"lookup": "peer_read"}'
+sglang serve --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tp-size 8 --attn-dp-size 8 \
+  --engram-config '{"lookup": "peer_read"}'
 ```
 
 ## Choosing a configuration

@@ -98,12 +98,14 @@ def override(self, value: Any):
         backup_value = os.environ.get(self.name)
         backup_set_to_none = self._set_to_none
         self.set(value)
-        yield
-        if backup_present:
-            os.environ[self.name] = backup_value
-        else:
-            os.environ.pop(self.name, None)
-        self._set_to_none = backup_set_to_none
+        try:
+            yield
+        finally:
+            if backup_present:
+                os.environ[self.name] = backup_value
+            else:
+                os.environ.pop(self.name, None)
+            self._set_to_none = backup_set_to_none
 
     def clear(self):
         os.environ.pop(self.name, None)
